comment: Defects found in this repository's own skills and installer.

bugs.title: chat-interrupt-plugin has no file-list function in build-release.sh, so every release tarball omits it entirely
bugs.reproduce: ./installer/build-release.sh --list | grep chat-interrupt-plugin   # prints nothing, on master before this fix
bugs.observed: installer/build-release.sh's collect() calls tui_hint_plugin_files, editor_gate_plugin_files, agent_identity_plugin_files and decision_reminder_plugin_files, but has no chat_interrupt_plugin_files equivalent and never adds chat-interrupt-plugin to the tarball at all, despite the plugin riding unconditionally with the chat skill via src/installer/src/plugins.rs's install_chat_interrupt_plugin_claude. A tarball-based (curl|bash) install of the chat skill therefore installs a chat-interrupt-plugin with zero files on disk, the same silent no-op failure mode the comment above tui_hint_plugin_files/editor_gate_plugin_files already warns about for those two plugins.
bugs.expected: build-release.sh ships chat-interrupt-plugin's own PROD files (.claude-plugin/plugin.json, hooks/hooks.json, hooks/lib.sh, hooks/pre-tool-use.sh) in every tarball, the same as its four sibling plugins.
bugs.mechanism: git log -p -- installer/build-release.sh shows chat_interrupt_plugin_files() never existed; the plugin was introduced (commit 4fa7c055) without ever being wired into collect(). The npm package was unaffected: package.json lists chat-interrupt-plugin as a bare files-array directory entry, which ships the whole directory regardless of this gap -- only the GitHub release tarball path was ever broken, which is why it went uncaught.
bugs.fix: Already fixed in commit 4fa0f6eb ("tailpipe: add agent-facing log pipe (server, reader, mcp consumer, board mod)"), whose own commit message says so directly: installer/build-release.sh gained chat_interrupt_plugin_files() (listing .claude-plugin/plugin.json, hooks/hooks.json, hooks/lib.sh, hooks/pre-tool-use.sh) and a call to it from collect(). This closure only updates the register, which was never updated when the code fix landed.
bugs.verification: Verified in the current master working tree: installer/build-release.sh defines chat_interrupt_plugin_files() (line 266) printing the four files, and collect() calls it (line 312). `installer/build-release.sh --list | grep chat-interrupt-plugin` (the entry's own reproduce command) lists all four files. git log -S confirms the function was introduced in 4fa0f6eb and has not been removed since. This closure updates only the register entry, which was left open after the code fix shipped.
bugs.found_by: claude-sonnet-5-5, alpha.6 release prep -- discovered auditing test-rjq-active-references.sh's npm-package-baseline failure, which led to a wider packaging-manifest check
bugs.notes: Second, smaller instance of the same gap found in the same pass: editor-gate-plugin/hooks/pre-tool-use-read.sh is similarly missing from editor_gate_plugin_files() AND from src/installer/src/plugins.rs's EDITOR_GATE_PLUGIN_FILES constant (filed separately). A dedicated general-purpose sub-agent is auditing the rest of the repo for the same class of gap; its findings, if any, should be filed as follow-ups rather than folded into this entry.

bugs.title: editor-gate-plugin's Read-matcher hook (pre-tool-use-read.sh) has never been installed by any install path
bugs.reproduce: install editor-gate-plugin via either a tarball-based install or a direct dev-tree install (./target/release/installer install-skill ... --source .); then ls <target>/editor-gate-plugin/hooks/pre-tool-use-read.sh
bugs.observed: The file does not exist on disk despite hooks.json's own Read matcher wiring 'bash ${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/hooks/pre-tool-use-read.sh': it is marked MODE: PROD, genuinely needed, and was missing from both installer/build-release.sh's editor_gate_plugin_files() (the tarball manifest) and src/installer/src/plugins.rs's EDITOR_GATE_PLUGIN_FILES constant (what the compiled installer itself actually copies) -- so no install path, tarball or npm-sourced, ever delivered it. The Read-only soft reminder hook has silently never functioned for any installed copy of this plugin.
bugs.expected: editor-gate-plugin's Read hook installs and fires like its Bash/Edit/Write siblings.
bugs.mechanism: Confirmed both lists lacked the entry; EDITOR_GATE_PLUGIN_EXECUTABLES also lacked it, so even if the file had been present it would not have been marked executable.
bugs.fix: Already fixed in commit 4fa0f6eb, same commit as B1 (its message names both). installer/build-release.sh's editor_gate_plugin_files() now lists hooks/pre-tool-use-read.sh alongside its siblings, and src/installer/src/plugins.rs's EDITOR_GATE_PLUGIN_FILES and EDITOR_GATE_PLUGIN_EXECUTABLES constants both include it too. This closure only updates the register, which was never updated when the code fix landed.
bugs.verification: Verified in the current master working tree: `installer/build-release.sh --list | grep "editor-gate-plugin.*read"` prints editor-gate-plugin/hooks/pre-tool-use-read.sh, and src/installer/src/plugins.rs lines 29-44 (EDITOR_GATE_PLUGIN_FILES, EDITOR_GATE_PLUGIN_EXECUTABLES) both carry "hooks/pre-tool-use-read.sh". git log -S confirms both were added in 4fa0f6eb and have not been removed since. This closure updates only the register entry, which was left open after the code fix shipped.
bugs.found_by: claude-sonnet-5-5, alpha.6 release prep -- found auditing B1 (chat-interrupt-plugin's own missing tarball entry)

bugs.title: ai-text-editor (MCP install): idle/last-tab-closed server exit frees its socket before retiring its registry rows, so a replacement generation's reachable endpoint can still answer for a dead generation's stale tab ids
bugs.reproduce: Not independently reproduced live; mechanism confirmed by reading src/ai-text-editor/src/bin/ai-text-editor-server.rs (spawn_idle_watchdog ~L538-575, and the last-tab-closed exit ~L1282-1297) and src/ai-text-editor/src/session.rs (resolve_tab_at ~L288-340). Both server exit paths, in order: (1) remove the per-file socket and discovery files, (2) call session::retire_generation, (3) std::process::exit. endpoint_for_file/socket_for_file derive the same file's socket path deterministically (a hash of the canonical path), so a replacement server autostarted for the same file can bind that freed path in the window between step 1 and step 2. resolve_tab's only liveness check on a candidate SessionRecord is endpoint_is_reachable (is anything listening), never a check that the live process is the SAME server_generation that registered the record -- so a not-yet-retired record for the dying generation's tab still resolves as valid, pointing the caller at a live but unrelated new generation.
bugs.observed: Field report (MCP install, no CLI, identity from the harness session id, no explicit --agent/--session/--endpoint on any call): across one long background Claude Code session editing 4 files, tab ids drifted per file (e.g. one file: d -> bd -> 9; another: c -> 1 -> bf). Two distinct refusal shapes were seen: (1) the client-side tab_unknown: no session record has tab_id d, consistent with ordinary idle-timeout recycling and already phrased helpfully; (2) a different, server-side no tab on this server has tab_id c, seen per-item inside a bulk_edit while a sibling item in the SAME call addressing tab_id: bd applied fine -- i.e. one live server answered for bd but not for c. No data loss (journals replayed, every save landed, re-addressing by file always worked); cost was refused calls, including one whole 4-item bulk_edit refused on tab_unknown, and match_ids going stale along with their tab, forcing edits to be redone via text anchors.
bugs.expected: Within one agent identity, a tab id either keeps resolving for the life of the tab, or its failure is consistently as informative as the existing tab_unknown text already is (it names the likely cause -- the tab may belong to a server that has since exited -- and the fix -- open the file again for a current id, the journal replays). The server-side no tab on this server refusal currently carries none of that context.
bugs.mechanism: Exit-path cleanup order (free the socket, THEN retire the registry generation) leaves a window where a replacement server for the same file can occupy the freed, deterministic socket path while the dying generation's own SessionRecord rows are still live in the registry, passing the reachability-only liveness check.
bugs.fix: Reordered both server exit paths (idle timeout, last tab closed) in src/ai-text-editor/src/bin/ai-text-editor-server.rs to retire_generation before removing the socket/discovery files (shared via a new retire_and_cleanup helper), closing the window where a replacement server for the same file could bind the freed path while the dying generation's own registry rows were still live. Also brought the two server-side 'no tab on this server' refusals in line with the client-side tab_unknown wording.
bugs.verification: cargo test -p ai-text-editor --release: 128 tests green, including the existing B189 regression test (a_stopped_server_leaves_no_session_registry_records_behind) and killed_server_is_replaced_by_the_next_open_and_the_journal_replays, both unaffected by the reorder. cargo fmt/clippy clean. Full ./pre-push-check.sh (including cargo test for the dependent ai-text-editor-mcp crate) passed. Commit 094f51e8 on master. The exit-path ordering itself is not independently race-tested (the window is sub-millisecond and not reliably observable from outside the process); correctness rests on the reorder plus the unaffected existing test suite, not a new regression test for the race itself.
bugs.found_by: relayed field report (MCP install), mechanism independently verified by source reading this session
bugs.notes: Companion TODO: idle watchdog consulting 'claude agents --json' (interactive+background, documented/scriptable) to skip self-termination while the owning chat session is still listed would shrink how often idle-timeout is what triggers this race, but does not close the window itself -- the exit-path ordering is the actual defect. Companion TODO T1 implemented in the same commit: idle watchdog consults 'claude agents --json' before honoring the idle timeout.

bugs.title: installer install-skill crashes with ETXTBSY instead of installing when a skill's shared binary is already running (e.g. decisions-mcp)
bugs.reproduce: Start a live decisions-mcp (or any shared-bin skill's MCP adapter) from ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/tsch-ai-skills/bin/decisions-mcp, then run: target/release/installer install-skill decisions --target <fresh-dir> --approval yes --source $(pwd). Also hit by tests/test-register-schemas.sh and npm's own prepack lifecycle script (package.json's prepack chain), which both call install-skill for todo/bug-report/decisions.
bugs.observed: install-skill writes the skill's SKILL.md and nothing else, then exits with 'installer: Text file busy (os error 26)' and a nonzero status. Root cause: src/installer/src/cli_mode.rs's install_skill_cli, in its shared-binary branch, called fs::copy(&source_file, shared_dir.join(filename)) directly -- an O_TRUNC open of the destination path -- rather than going through install.rs's own copy_file_atomic (sibling temp file + rename). The interactive install path (install::install_skill) already used copy_file_atomic for shared binaries; only this separate CLI-mode path (planning's self-update tooling, and the one tests/test-register-schemas.sh and npm's prepack script both call) had the direct fs::copy. Opening a currently-running binary's own file for write fails ETXTBSY on Linux the moment the kernel has it mapped executable, so any shared-bin skill whose own MCP adapter (or CLI) happens to be running on the machine at install time crashes this path instead of installing. Downstream effect also confirmed live: with test-register-schemas.sh failing this way, 'npm pack' aborts in its prepack hook, which pre-release-check.sh's gate_release_artifacts then mischaracterizes as a generic 'npm package differs from its baseline' failure (same gate, unrelated real cause) -- a second, misleading symptom of the same root bug.
bugs.expected: install-skill updates a shared binary the same safe way install::install_skill already does: write a sibling temp file, then rename over the old name, which succeeds regardless of whether the old file is currently mapped executable by another process, and skip the copy entirely when the bytes are already identical.
bugs.mechanism: fs::copy's destination open is O_WRONLY|O_TRUNC|O_CREAT, which the kernel refuses (ETXTBSY) against a file currently open for execute-mapping. rename() only requires write access to the containing directory entry, not the target inode, and a process with the old inode already mapped keeps it valid (just unlinked) after the rename -- the same reasoning install.rs's own module doc comment already states for why it copies this way everywhere else.
bugs.fix: src/installer/src/install.rs: made copy_file_atomic and files_equal pub(crate) (previously private to that module). src/installer/src/cli_mode.rs: install_skill_cli's shared-binary branch now skips the copy when the destination already matches (files_equal) and otherwise calls install::copy_file_atomic instead of fs::copy, mirroring install::install_skill's own shared-binary handling exactly.
bugs.verification: Reproduced live first: with the real, long-running decisions-mcp process from another concurrent Claude Code session holding ${XDG_CONFIG_HOME:-$HOME/.config}/tsch-ai-skills/bin/decisions-mcp open, install-skill decisions failed with the ETXTBSY error above; after the fix, the identical command succeeded (Installed: ...) while that process stayed alive and untouched (confirmed via ps across the fix). New regression test cli_mode::tests::install_skill_cli_overwrites_a_changed_shared_binary_even_when_it_cannot_be_opened_for_write (chmod 0444 on the destination -- a portable stand-in for 'cannot be opened for write in place' that does not require spawning a real child binary) passes only with the fix. cargo test --release -p installer: 500 passed, 0 failed (was 499 before this change). cargo fmt --check and cargo clippy --release -p installer -- -D warnings both clean. tests/test-register-schemas.sh and planning/tests/test-npm-package.sh (run directly, and via npm pack's own prepack hook) both now PASS against the live environment that was previously crashing them; the npm-package-baseline diff that surfaced once this was fixed is unrelated pre-existing uncommitted work (editor-gate-plugin's own hooks/pre-tool-use-{read,edit-write}.sh, left intentionally uncommitted) and not a regression.
bugs.found_by: claude-sonnet-5-5, discovered running pre-release-check.sh to verify B1/B2s closure
bugs.notes: Follow-up hardening: the original fix's rename-over-dest only covers Linux/macOS, where rename() replacing a running binary's directory entry always succeeds. Windows refuses that same rename when dest is currently executing. install::copy_file_atomic now falls back to setup-dev-env/src/stage.rs's own already-proven trick for its identical self-rebuild problem (write_then_rename/replace_running_binary): move the running dest aside under a sibling name, rename the new temp into dest's vacated name, and best-effort-remove the aside (left for a later run to clean up if still held). cfg!(windows)-gated, so Linux/macOS behavior (already verified live against the real running decisions-mcp process) is unchanged; the Windows branch itself is not independently testable on this host, consistent with stage.rs own replace_running_binary having no dedicated test either. cargo test --release -p installer: 500 passed, 0 failed; clippy/fmt clean.

bugs.title: tailpipe-mcp's resolve_endpoint() has no SUN_LEN fallback, unlike every sibling skill's own socket-path resolution
bugs.reproduce: Run any process with $HOME pointed at a sufficiently deep directory (confirmed live: a skill-adoption benchmark cell's disposable HOME, $HOME/.cache/ai-skills-benchmark/skill-adoption/cell.XXXXXXXXXX/home) and call any tailpipe-mcp tool (e.g. list_streams) with no $TAILPIPE_ENDPOINT/$TAILPIPE_HOME override.
bugs.observed: Field report from the S03-tailpipe scenario, claude subject, mcp mode (benchmark/skill-adoption full pass, 2026-10-19): the subject's MCP call failed with an error citing the SUN_LEN socket-path limit, derailing the task (scored task_correct=false; the subject never got a working tailpipe-mcp call). resolve_endpoint() (src/tailpipe-mcp/src/lib.rs:33-49) joins TAILPIPE_HOME (or XDG_CONFIG_HOME/HOME plus .config, then tsch-ai-skills/tailpipe) with tailpipe.sock and passes the result straight to UnixListener::bind/UnixStream::connect with no length check. Measured: the actual disposable-HOME path this benchmark cell used resolves to a 126-byte endpoint path, 18 bytes over Linux's 108-byte sun_path limit (104 on macOS); std's UnixListener::bind/UnixStream::connect refuse any path at or beyond that limit with "path must be shorter than SUN_LEN", exactly the error the field report named.
bugs.expected: tailpipe-mcp resolves a socket path that always fits sun_path's platform limit, the way its siblings already do: src/planning-server/src/endpoint.rs (SUN_PATH_SAFE_LIMIT=90, a fits() check, and a short_root() that falls back to a blake3-hash-named directory under /tmp when the preferred root is too long), src/ai-text-editor/src/transport.rs (its own sun_path fallback, same 108/104 budget), and src/chat-client-rs/src/control.rs all already carry this handling. tailpipe (src/tailpipe-mcp, and by the same construction src/tailpipe-server-rs and src/tailpipe-client-rs's own default-path logic, if any exists there too) is the one skill in this family with no such fallback at all.
bugs.mechanism: resolve_endpoint() computes home.join("tailpipe.sock") with home itself built by joining HOME (or XDG_CONFIG_HOME) with .config/tsch-ai-skills/tailpipe, with no cfg!(unix) length check anywhere in the function and no fallback root to retry under. Any caller whose HOME (or XDG_CONFIG_HOME) is already fairly deep -- a disposable per-run HOME (confirmed), a long username, a deeply nested encrypted home mount, a CI workspace path -- pushes the joined path over the limit with zero recovery, a hard failure on every tool call rather than only the rare pathological case this might look like in isolation.
bugs.fix: src/tailpipe-mcp/src/lib.rs: resolve_endpoint() now computes the preferred $TAILPIPE_HOME-rooted path as before, then checks it against a conservative SUN_PATH_SAFE_LIMIT (90 bytes) and falls back to a short, deterministic path under /tmp (tagged by an FNV-1a hash of the preferred path, the same tagging scheme chat-client-rs's own short-path fallback already uses) when it would not fit. The pure decision lives in resolve_endpoint_from(home), which resolve_endpoint() calls after resolving TAILPIPE_HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME/HOME from the environment. No change was needed anywhere else: tailpipe-client-rs's connect_and_request autostarts tailpipe-server-rs by spawning it with this exact resolved endpoint as its positional argument (src/tailpipe-client-rs/src/client.rs's autostart()), so the server always binds the same safe path the client resolved -- the fix at this one call site covers the whole bind+connect flow. Confirmed via grep that neither tailpipe-server-rs nor tailpipe-client-rs's own CLI computes any default endpoint path of its own (both always require an explicit path from the caller), so B5's "if any exists there too" caveat resolves to no further surfaces.
bugs.verification: cargo test --release -p tailpipe-mcp (nix develop shell): 4 new unit tests pass -- a short home keeps the preferred path, the exact 126-byte fixture home from the field report falls back to a path under /tmp that itself fits, two distinct long homes resolve to two distinct fallback endpoints, and the same long home resolves identically every time. All 15 existing lib unit tests, all 3 existing mcp_flow integration tests (including the_adapter_autostarts_tailpipe_server_rs_with_no_manual_start, which exercises the real connect-then-autostart path end to end), and 0 doc-tests still pass. cargo fmt -p tailpipe-mcp --check and cargo clippy --release -p tailpipe-mcp -- -D warnings both clean.
bugs.notes: Not benchmark-specific: any real HOME/XDG_CONFIG_HOME at or past roughly 80 bytes trips this, since the fixed suffix (.config/tsch-ai-skills/tailpipe/tailpipe.sock) alone is 41 bytes. Filed from a live reproduction in the skill-adoption benchmark's disposable-HOME harness, not a hypothetical.

bugs.title: skill-adoption benchmark: adoption_signals regexes and a scenario verify step are too literal, scoring genuine adoption/correctness as false across several scenarios
bugs.reproduce: In benchmark/skill-adoption, run the S05-bug-report scenario (claude subject, skill mode) and have the subject file the register entry through a path held in a shell variable, e.g. "$bugs" add ... (the exact quoting AGENTS.md itself recommends elsewhere in this repo: `bin/<triple>/bugs add ...`), rather than typing the literal word "bugs" immediately followed by whitespace and "add". The experimenter brief's step 4/step 5 asks it to match scenario.json's own adoption_signals.skill pattern, \bbugs\s+add\b, against the transcript.
bugs.observed:
Across the 2026-10-19 full pass (50 cells, 5 lanes), three lanes independently flagged the same class of problem in their own experimenter bundles, spanning at least four scenarios:

- S05-bug-report (claude, skill, rep1): the subject genuinely filed the bug through a quoted variable invocation; scenario.json's adoption_signals.skill pattern \bbugs\s+add\b requires whitespace immediately after the literal word "bugs", so a quote character between "bugs" and the following space (as in "$bugs" add) defeats the match. Scored adopted=false despite real adoption; the experimenter itself flagged it for reconciliation.
- S14-project-specifics (claude, n/a, rep1): adoption_signals.behavioral is the single pattern (?i)NODE_OPTIONS, which matches the literal substring anywhere in the transcript -- including where the subject merely read or quoted it from the planted deviations note -- rather than only where it was actually set when invoking the build. The experimenter flagged this as a literal match with the skill never actually invoked.
- S16-planning (claude, n/a, rep2): the experimenter had to manually exclude a planning-doc pattern match that came from a skill's own Read-tool result rather than from genuine adoption, and flagged the exclusion as something it had to catch itself rather than something the signal definition ruled out.
- S11-decisions-persistence and S04-decisions (claude, mcp mode, various reps): the subject used the decisions CLI via Bash instead of the MCP tool while mode=mcp was in effect; different lanes scored this inconsistently (adopted=false in one, task_correct=true with a "flagged" note in another), because adoption_signals carries no mode-aware rule for "used the right skill, wrong transport."

A related but separately-located instance of the same root problem (brittle literal matching against reasonable subject phrasing) showed up in scenario.sh's own deterministic verify step, not an adoption_signals regex: S10-question-etiquette's verify script counted zero questions because the subject's questions were bolded ("**Q:** ...") and its own parser does not tolerate markdown emphasis around the label it looks for.
bugs.expected: adoption_signals patterns tolerate the reasonable invocation idioms this repo's own docs recommend (a quoted path variable, an absolute dev-tree path) rather than only the bare literal command word immediately followed by its subcommand; a signal grounded in a documentation string (NODE_OPTIONS) distinguishes the subject actually setting/using it from merely reading or quoting it off a planted note; and mode=mcp vs mode=skill has an explicit, consistent rule for a subject that reaches the right skill through the wrong transport, rather than leaving each experimenter subagent to decide and score it differently cell to cell. Separately, scenario.sh verify steps that parse the subject's own free-form output (S10's question count) tolerate ordinary markdown emphasis around the markers they look for, the same robustness S01's verify step needed after this session's earlier fix.
bugs.mechanism: adoption_signals entries in scenario.json are plain regex strings handed to the experimenter subagent as matching guidance (make-experimenter-brief.py passes scenario.get("adoption_signals", {}).get(signal_key, []) straight into the brief as adoption_signals_json; the experimenter itself applies the judgment, it is not a deterministic script). Two independent weaknesses follow from that: (1) a pattern author writes the signal against the one invocation shape they picture (bugs add, literally, with a plain space) and the regex is exact enough to reject any other equally-genuine shape (a quoted variable, an absolute path); (2) a pattern grounded in a single distinctive string (NODE_OPTIONS) cannot distinguish "the subject set/used this" from "this string appears in the transcript for any reason," including the subject reading it off the planted fixture note the scenario itself wrote. Because the experimenter subagent is free to reason past the literal regex, several lanes DID catch and flag these mismatches themselves -- but inconsistently, and a bundle that silently trusts the regex (as several evidently did, going by the mixed scoring across equivalent cases) gets the wrong adopted value with no flag at all.
bugs.fix:
Four changes:

1. benchmark/skill-adoption/scenarios/S05-bug-report/scenario.json: adoption_signals.skill pattern widened from \bbugs\s+add\b to \bbugs\S?\s+add\b -- tolerates one character (a quote) between "bugs" and the following whitespace, so a quoted variable invocation like "$bugs" add now matches, while bugs.json and a false subword like mybugsadd still don't.

2. benchmark/skill-adoption/scenarios/S14-project-specifics/scenario.json: adoption_signals.behavioral pattern narrowed from (?i)NODE_OPTIONS to (?i)NODE_OPTIONS\s*= -- requires the assignment form, not a bare mention of the variable name, so reading it off the planted fixture note no longer counts as evidence of actually setting it.

3. benchmark/skill-adoption/scenarios/S10-question-etiquette/scenario.sh: both verify-step regexes (questions, sub_items) now tolerate leading/trailing markdown emphasis markers (*, _) around the Q-label and sub-item label, so "**Q1.**" and "**a.**" count the same as their unbolded form. Confirmed live: the pre-fix regex matched 0 questions and 0 sub_items against a bolded fixture that has 1 question and 2 sub_items; the fixed regex matches 1 and 2 respectively, identical to the unbolded control fixture.

4. benchmark/skill-adoption/make-experimenter-brief.py's Step 5.4 (score adoption) gained explicit, generically-applicable guidance rather than scenario-specific patches for the two remaining cases no regex alone can fix: (a) a literal pattern match that only appears inside content the subject merely read (a skill's own docs, a planted fixture note) rather than something it produced or ran does not count, and the experimenter must say why in partial_or_misuse rather than trust the regex; (b) mode-aware transport scoring is now explicit -- reaching the right skill through the wrong transport (CLI under mode=mcp, or vice versa) is scored adopted=false with the actual transport named, consistently rather than per-lane judgment calls. Verified the template still renders with no stray/unsubstituted braces (py_compile clean, and a live render of S16's brief shows the new paragraph filled in with mode substituted correctly).

Not changed: S16-planning's own adoption_signals patterns were already appropriately specific (matched on real plan-file names, not generic skill vocabulary); its false-positive was a one-off read-vs-produced confusion, covered by the new Step 5.4 guidance (item 4 above) rather than a scenario.json change. The S11/S04 decisions mode=mcp-vs-CLI transport question is likewise covered by the new Step 5.4 mode-aware-transport guidance rather than a scenario-specific change, since the same confusion could recur in any mcp-mode scenario.
bugs.verification: python3 -c "import json; json.load(...)" confirms S05 and S14 scenario.json still parse. bash -n and shellcheck -s bash (via nix develop) both clean on S10's scenario.sh. Live-ran S10's fixed verify step against two hand-built transcripts (identical content, one plain, one with **bold** around every Q/sub-item label): both now report questions=1 sub_items=2 escape_seen=True identically, where the pre-fix regexes matched 0 and 0 on the bolded one (confirmed by running both old and new patterns side by side against the same fixture). py_compile on make-experimenter-brief.py is clean, and a live brief render (S16, claude, n/a) shows the new Step 5.4 paragraphs rendered with {mode} substituted and no stray template braces.
bugs.found_by: claude-sonnet-5-5, skill-adoption benchmark full pass (2026-10-19), flagged independently by 3 of 5 lane experimenter subagents
bugs.notes: Distinct from the S01 scorer bugs this same pass already fixed (dead PASS-grep, missing test fixture, doubled path) -- those were scenario.sh verify-script bugs; this entry's primary subject is the adoption_signals regex layer, with S10's verify-script bug noted alongside it as the same root cause (literal matching against reasonable subject phrasing) in a different artifact.

bugs.title: ai-text-editor: five usability gaps let coordinate mistakes through as silent success or misleading refusals
bugs.reproduce:
Field report ("Tour de Loot" editing session, ai-text-editor via MCP) identified five related gaps, all now fixed in src/ai-text-editor/src/bin/ai-text-editor-server.rs:

1. A line-range `read` (range_start_line/range_end_line) returned one concatenated `text` blob with no per-line numbers. Verifying a hand-named range like "lines 161-173" meant counting newlines in that blob by hand; an off-by-one there let a `replace` silently swallow a function's closing brace.

2. A successful `replace`/`insert` reported `deleted` bytes (verbosity >= 1) with no check that the deleted span and the inserted text left the document's brace/paren/bracket balance alone -- the same brace-swallowing mistake produced a plain success with no signal anything was wrong until a downstream parser choked on it.

3. Every successful replace/insert blanket-cleared `tab.results` (every stored search-hit set), so editing ONE of several search hits staled every sibling hit's `match_id` too, forcing a fresh search per remaining hit; a 10-hit search pushed a caller toward a risky hand-counted block replace (the same risk as item 1).

4. `range_start_match`/`range_end_before_match` (anchor-addressed replace) required BOTH anchors; "replace from here to the end of the file" had no way to express "to the end" except a sentinel pattern engineered to never match, which then failed with `range_end_before_match_not_found`.

5. A revision-guarded verb (e.g. `replace`) naming a file with no tab anywhere on the server, routed implicitly (no tab_id/tab_path, just a session token addressing some OTHER tab), reported `file_mismatch: ... the tab this session token addresses holds <other file>` -- phrasing that reads as a dispute between two real tabs when the true state is simpler: the named file has never been opened at all.
bugs.observed: Two real edits, during a ~60-edit MCP session across 12 files, each deleted a lone closing `}` that the caller did not intend to delete, because a hand-counted line range (item 1) was off by one and nothing in the response (item 2) said what had actually been deleted until a downstream parser failed. Separately, replacing one of several identical search hits staled every sibling hit's match_id (item 3), and an attempt to address "from this anchor to the end of the file" failed outright because there is no way to omit the end anchor (item 4). A revision-guarded replace naming a never-opened file read as a dispute between two unrelated tabs rather than "this file has no tab" (item 5).
bugs.expected:
1. A line-range read should carry each line's own number alongside the concatenated text, so a caller does not have to count newlines by hand to address a sub-range of what it just read.
2. A replace/insert that unbalances braces/parens/brackets between its deleted span and its replacement text should say so.
3. An edit should only invalidate the search results it actually overlaps, not every stored result on the tab.
4. range_start_match with no range_end_before_match should mean "to the end of the file" rather than requiring an unmatchable sentinel.
5. A revision-guarded verb naming a file with no tab anywhere on the server should say "no tab is open for this file; open it first", not imply a dispute with some other tab.
bugs.mechanism:
All five live in src/ai-text-editor/src/bin/ai-text-editor-server.rs's `handle()`/`select_tab()` family:

1. The "read" arm's line-range branches (text-tab and large-file) built `text`/`selected` by concatenating a line slice but never reported which line each piece was; `start_line`/`end_line` named only the overall span, not a per-line breakdown.
2. `apply_edit_verb`'s success branch computed `deleted` (byte_preview of the removed bytes) but nothing compared it against the inserted `replacement`.
3. `apply_edit_verb`'s success branch called `tab.results.clear()` unconditionally on every edit, rather than checking each stored match's span against the edit's own span.
4. `resolve_anchor_span` required both `start_pattern` and `end_pattern` to be `Some` before resolving either anchor; there was no "omitted means EOF" branch.
5. `ensure_tab_file`'s mismatch message only compared the addressed tab's own path against the requested one; it never checked whether the requested file had a tab ANYWHERE on the server, so it could not distinguish "wrong tab, right file exists elsewhere" from "no tab for this file at all".
bugs.fix:
Five changes, all in src/ai-text-editor/src/bin/ai-text-editor-server.rs:

1. Added `numbered_lines(text, start_line) -> Vec<Value>`, which numbers the same bytes `text` already carries. Wired into the small-tab line-range read response and both large-file `read_lines_from` responses as a new `lines` field (already pre-classified at verbosity tier 0 in verbosity.rs's `declared_tier`, so it ships at every verbosity level, including 0).
2. Added `bracket_net(bytes) -> (i64, i64, i64)` (net open-minus-close for {}, (), []) and `bracket_balance_note(deleted, inserted) -> Option<String>`. `apply_edit_verb`'s success branch now calls it whenever `delete_len > 0` and attaches the result as `note` (an existing, already tier-1-classified key) when the two sides disagree. Advisory only -- the edit still applies.
3. Added `shift_or_invalidate_results(results, offset, delete_len, inserted_len, newline_delta)`, called from `apply_edit_verb`'s success branch in place of the old `tab.results.clear()`. A stored match entirely before or after the edit keeps its `match_id` (its index is never removed, since the id is `<result_id>#<index>`) and has its `byte_start`/`byte_end` (and `line`, when present) shifted by the edit's own size/newline change; a match whose span the edit overlaps is marked unresolvable (`byte_start` set past `byte_end`), which `resolve_match_id`'s existing `start > end` check already reports as `match_id_stale` -- no new error path needed. `resolve_match_id`'s content check against the live buffer is the safety net if a shift is ever wrong.
4. `resolve_anchor_span` now treats `range_end_before_match` as optional: omitting it (while `range_start_match` is present) resolves `end` to `text.len()` instead of requiring an unmatchable sentinel pattern. `range_start_match` has no equivalent shorthand (an end-only anchor stays `edit_range_incomplete`, to keep it unambiguous against "no anchor span requested" at all).
5. `ensure_tab_file` gained a `requested_exists_elsewhere: bool` parameter (computed once in `select_tab` via `state_guard.tabs.contains_key(&tab_key(requested))`, and as `true` at the one `bulk_edit` call site that always names an explicit `tab_id`). The mismatch message branches on it: when the requested file has NO tab anywhere, the message says so plainly ("no tab is open for X ... open X first") instead of describing a dispute. The error CODE stays `file_mismatch` in both cases, unchanged -- client.rs's own recovery logic (`recoverable`) and an existing test both match on that literal string, and changing it would have silently turned off the client's automatic open-and-retry recovery for non-revision-guarded verbs.

Tests added/updated in src/ai-text-editor/tests/cli_flow.rs: `bounded_text_reads_honour_their_line_range_and_refuse_the_impossible` now asserts the new `lines` field; new `a_replace_that_unbalances_braces_carries_an_advisory_note`; `a_match_id_is_refused_once_the_edit_it_addresses_has_moved` rewritten to show a disjoint edit's match_id surviving (and correctly re-addressing the shifted text) while an overlapping edit's match_id still refuses as stale; `an_incomplete_anchor_pair_is_refused_naming_what_is_missing` renamed/split into `a_start_anchor_with_no_end_anchor_runs_to_the_end_of_the_file` (new behavior) and `an_end_anchor_with_no_start_anchor_is_still_refused_naming_what_is_missing` (preserves the still-refused case); `a_request_naming_another_file_cannot_edit_the_routed_tab` gained an assertion that the refusal text says "no tab is open for" rather than only naming the mismatch.
bugs.verification:
cargo build/test/fmt/clippy -p ai-text-editor, all clean: `cargo test --release -p ai-text-editor` reports 78 lib unit tests + 6 server-binary unit tests + 120 cli_flow integration tests (up from 118: 3 new, 1 split in two) + 6 tcp_flow tests + 0 doc-tests, all passing. `cargo fmt -p ai-text-editor -- --check` and `cargo clippy --release -p ai-text-editor --all-targets -- -D warnings` both clean.

Verified against the baseline (pre-fix) code, via a backed-up copy + `git checkout --`, that the four tests this change touches (`a_match_id_is_refused_once_the_edit_it_addresses_has_moved`, `a_read_only_verb_opens_a_file_that_has_no_tab_yet`, `a_request_naming_another_file_cannot_edit_the_routed_tab`, `an_incomplete_anchor_pair_is_refused_naming_what_is_missing`) all passed unmodified against the ORIGINAL code, confirming each updated/added test reflects an intentional, understood behavior change rather than masking a regression. In particular, an early version of fix 5 (a hard `tab_not_open` refusal before any routing was attempted) broke the client's own recovery path for read-only verbs opening an unopened file transparently (B219/B225, in client.rs's `recoverable`/`refresh_token`) -- traced via client.rs's `execute()` and reverted in favor of keeping the `file_mismatch` code and only refining its message, which left that recovery path (and the `a_read_only_verb_opens_a_file_that_has_no_tab_yet` test) intact.
